subject: POC readiness: sequenced MAP for environment gating & closure
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC readiness: sequenced MAP for environment gating & closure

Hi Amelia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited by the use cases you outlined. Per our conversation, attaching a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) that sequences the POC environment tasks so we can both track blockers and align on a close-by date.

High-level timeline (target: 2-week POC starting next Monday):
- Day 0–1: org setup & API key provisioning (we create the Redwood org and service user; you accept invite)
- Day 2–3: IP allowlist + short-lived API key validation
- Day 4–6: VPC peering attempt + small inference smoke tests
- Day 7–10: workload-run evals, latency/cost checkpoints
- Day 11–14: wrap, evaluation readout, and go/no-go decision

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Confirm a point-of-contact for network/VPC peering (cc'd DevOps works, if that's the right alias).
2) Share an IP block for allowlisting (CIDR) and a preferred maintenance window for peering.
3) Accept the Redwood org invite we will send by EOD today.

Attached: nexa_map_v1.xlsx (MAP w/ ownership columns) — it includes specific API-key names we will issue and a proposed canary model for smoke tests.

I'll loop in Connor for the peering steps and Vivek for SLA/commit questions if we need to fast-track a dedicated slot.

Thanks —

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: nexa_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 48 KB)
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@nexahealth.com>

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for this. The timeline looks good but we need to compress the window: our clinical team wants a results summary within 10 business days. Can we target a 10-business-day cadence instead of two weeks?

Quick answers:
- Point-of-contact for VPC peering: Javier Ortiz (he's on the DevOps alias).
- IP block: 203.0.113.0/24 (temporary for the POC)
- Maintenance window: preferred after 18:00 ET on weekdays.

I'll accept the org invite once I see it. Please put the VPC peering steps in writing so I can pass to Javier.

Best,
Amelia Ross
Head of Platform Integrations
NexaHealth
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC readiness: sequenced MAP for environment gating & closure

Hi Amelia — looping in the peering checklist below so Javier has a runnable sequence. I'll also attach a simple network diagram and a peering template for signature.

Minimal VPC peering steps (POC-focused):
1) Provide your VPC ID and the CIDR to be used (you gave 203.0.113.0/24 — we'll add that to our allowlist).
2) Confirm the AWS account ID we should target for the peering request.
3) We propose symmetric route table entries in the POC subnets (we can script this if you prefer).
4) We'll perform an initial small inference run (10-20 short requests) through the peered route during your maintenance window — we expect <150ms median RTT for 512-token requests on our verified canary model.
5) If the peering fails, fallback plan: we will issue a short-lived public API key scoped to your org and require only IP allowlist (no peering). This is faster but slightly higher network egress risk.

Attachments included:
- nexa_network_diagram.png (PNG, 120 KB)
- vpc_peering_template.docx (docx, 12 KB)

Next steps from Redwood:
- We will send the org invite now.
- Soojin will update the MAP to shrink the timeline to 10 business days and mark the peering and fallback as parallel tasks.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: nexa_network_diagram.png (png, 120 KB)

Thanks Connor — that checklist is perfect. Javier will review the docx and confirm the AWS account ID by EOD tomorrow. We're good to proceed with the compressed timeline; I'll accept the invite shortly.

One small ask: can the public API fallback keys be limited to 24-hour validity? That helps our security team sign off faster.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Amelia
